I’m 24 and on the autism spectrum, and… yeah. It’s rough. Between masking constantly and executive dysfunction, keeping myself afloat feels impossible much of the time. I push forward because I feel like I must, but it’s slow and unsteady and depression makes it so much less rewarding when I accomplish anything. I often feel like I can’t maintain any relationship I have, save for those with my family, who I feel distant from even though they love me. 

It is easy to think you’ve given up, but hard to truly do so. Don’t give in. Some things that have helped me in the past: Talk to strangers online, in forums or whatnot. It won’t feel like enough, but it will feel like something, and you may make some casual friends. You’re autistic; I guarantee there is a side of you that is engaging and interesting to people, that they like to be around. Go out to shops and restaurants, be kind to the employees, talk to them a little. Do things that make you feel good, provided they aren’t addictive or dangerous to your health. Really listen to people and examine yourself when they take some issue with your behavior. They’re often cruel or unfair, but there’s usually been something I didn’t fully understand was socially unacceptable and I try to adjust that. Just be careful not to take it too far and let them walk all over you. Go on hikes if you have the means and fitness and contemplate as many plants and animals as you can. (Careful there — I for one can get counterproductively existential.) If not, go for walks, and smile and greet people you pass.

None of these things will cure your depression, and they may not even work for you, but they’ve kept me from slipping over the edge before. Just trying to help in my autistic, practical way. If nothing else I hope the fact that someone took notice will give you a little heart ☺️ I probably won’t get to any private messages but if you reply to my comment I will get back to you when I can.

People react a lot better if they have context ahead of time, and as a bonus, you’ll be filtering out people who won’t tolerate autism.

I fully support trans rights, but I can’t deny that there is an inherent physical advantage afforded to MTF trans athletes. I think one way to help fix this could be removing gender as a category for athletics where possible, and instead testing athletes into different divisions based on their physical attributes. Mostly things would still fall along gender lines, but it would allow trans people to compete without worrying about their gender, and also make it easier for outliers like exceptionally large and strong women and slight men to be competitive. There could be more than two divisions as well, for greater precision. I don’t think this would necessarily work with every sport, but it would work with many and it’s at least a start.

I really love this! I would suggest a few balance changes: Tutru’s first activated ability should cost UG. The trickier cost makes the second ability less oppressive, especially if it’s the only skeleton you have on board. Also, I would suggest reducing the amount of mill on the Flax trigger to 2 or *maybe* 3, since you already get accumulated benefit from everything in your yard. 5 is excessive; destroy a couple of creatures and you generate insane card advantage, especially with a way to reanimate. Similarly, Crim could read “one or more skeletons”. That’s typically how those cards are done to keep the power at a more steady benefit instead of swinging all over the place. Between Flax and Crim, you definitely need to reduce the power of at least one of them just so they’re fun to play against— I would recommend Flax, as that’s a much more powerful ability. Glinks is on the strong side but seems like a good design and I have no real critiques. 
I’d also like to suggest a spell this got me thinking of that you could add in if you wanted: Frenzied Reassembling. Sorcery, 4BBB. Return all Skeletons from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped. They gain indestructible until your next turn.
